channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Paterno’s Pizza Gets New Owners, But ‘Heart And Soul’ Of Beloved NW Side Business Will Remain
item.description: Three generations of Paternos ran the Jefferson Park pizzeria, which began as a liquor store in 1954. The Patel family bought the restaurant and has pledged to "respect everything that made Paterno’s special."

item.title: Chicago Theatre Week Returns With 75 Shows Citywide. Here’s How To Get Discounted Tickets
item.description: Chicago Theater Week runs Feb. 5-15. Tickets are on sale for $30 or less at major and storefront theaters.

item.title: Mother McAuley Grad Abbey Murphy Heading To Olympics With 2026 US Women’s Hockey Team
item.description: The Evergreen Park native and Mother McAuley High School graduate was named last week to the 2026 U.S. Olympic Women's Hockey Team.

item.title: Judge To Hold Hearing On Border Patrol Agents’ Use Of Force
item.description: A federal judge is set to hold a hearing Thursday in a lawsuit challenging federal immigration enforcement actions in Chicago.

item.title: Work Begins To Turn Humboldt Park’s Pioneer Arcade Into Affordable Senior Apartments
item.description: Designed by architect Jens Jensen, the terra cotta-clad former arcade built in 1925 is a valuable part of Chicago’s immigrant history.

item.title: ‘Missing Middle’ Housing Program Breaks Ground On 1st Project In North Lawndale
item.description: The city initiative to rebuild middle-class housing on the South and West sides kicked off Tuesday with the construction of seven two-flats on formerly vacant lots.

item.title: What Happened To Linda Brown? Search Ramps Up For Missing Special Ed Teacher
item.description: Brown, a teacher a Robert Healy Elementary School, went missing Saturday. She was believed to be headed to an appointment in Wicker Park, but she never made it.

item.title: Report: Sexual Misconduct Widespread On Campus Where Former Dean Sentenced To 22 Years Worked
item.description: Seven other former teachers, administrators and staff at Greater Lawndale High School for Social Justice and at a school sharing a building with it also engaged in inappropriate behavior toward students, a CPS watchdog report found.

item.title: Chicago Authors, Neighbors Bid Farewell To Volumes Bookcafe At ‘Our Last Event’ Before Closure
item.description: The Wicker Park bookstore and cafe will close at the end of January after almost a decade in business. Owners said the opening of a nearby Barnes & Noble led to a sharp drop in sales over the past year.

item.title: ‘Time And Place’ Curfew Proposal Advances To City Council Vote
item.description: The latest proposal from Ald. Brian Hopkins would let police impose a four-hour "time and place" curfew anywhere in the city with advance notice, reviving a fight Mayor Brandon Johnson has already rejected once.
